entities.title: Run the browser locally
entities.summary: Serve the folder and open it with a repository's address.
steps: cd cyberspace-explorer
python3 -m http.server 8000
Open http://localhost:8000/?url=https://github.com/<owner>/<repository> in a browser
entities.verify: The folder tree and the first folder appear, and the browser's console shows no errors.
entities.details: Served this way there is no Worker, so there is no GitHub sign-in: the page offers a pasted token instead. The Worker itself is checked with `npm test` ([its verification](worker/.dev/verification.json)).

entities.title: Check this description
entities.summary: Run both validators from the repository root after changing a .dev file or an actor.
entities.when: After changing any .dev folder, Actors/ or Meta/Agents.
steps: pip install jsonschema
python3 Meta/Agents/Skills/validate_diagrams.py
python3 Meta/Agents/Knowledge/validate_knowledge.py
entities.verify: The first prints what it validated with no error; the second ends with 0 problems.
entities.details: `Meta/Agents/` is a copy of `Agents/` from human-assisted-software-development; the validators find their schemas next to themselves and scan the whole repository. See AGENTS.md.

entities.title: Publish a new version
entities.summary: Merge the change to main; the CI/CD container tests it and deploys it.
entities.when: When the owner wants a change live.
steps: Merge the change to main
Wait for the container to test it (the commit status ci/cyberspace-explorer) and deploy it (deploy/cyberspace-explorer); a poll takes up to a minute
To deploy by hand, or again, on the container's machine: docker compose run --rm ci deploy <sha> (add --force for a commit CI has not passed)
entities.verify: https://cyberspace-explorer.com shows the change; the deploy's last step checks that the page, /auth/me and /crawler answer, and rolls back if they don't.
entities.details: Nothing is deployed while the container's DEPLOY_ENABLED is false, or while wrangler.jsonc or crawler/wrangler.jsonc still holds REPLACE-WITH-D1-DATABASE-ID (crawler/README.md, "Setting it up once (the owner)"). The deploy's log is deploy-<sha>.log in the container's logs volume.

entities.title: Release cyberspace-generator
entities.summary: Push a generator-v* tag; the container builds the Linux half of the release, then release-macos.sh on the owner's Mac adds the macOS half and publishes it.
entities.when: When a change to crates/ should reach zazzle.
steps: Set version under [workspace.package] in Cargo.toml to the new version, and merge that to main
Tag the merged commit generator-v<that version> and push the tag: git tag generator-v<version> origin/main && git push origin generator-v<version>

Wait for the container (RELEASE_ENABLED=true) to build and test the Linux binaries and put them, with their SHA256SUMS lines, in a draft release of the tag; its log is release-generator-v<version>.log

On the Mac, from a checkout of continuous_integration_and_delivery: cyberspace-explorer/release-macos.sh generator-v<version>. It builds and tests the macOS binaries, adds them to the draft, completes SHA256SUMS and publishes the release
entities.verify: The release generator-v<version> is published with cyberspace-generator-aarch64-apple-darwin, -x86_64-apple-darwin, -x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, -aarch64-unknown-linux-musl and SHA256SUMS; zazzle's bump-cyberspace-generator.sh then offers it.
entities.details: The two halves can run in either order: whichever finds all four binaries in place publishes, and until then the release is a draft that zazzle does not see. A tag that does not match Cargo.toml is refused by both. Either half can be run again; a published release is never changed. Without RELEASE_ENABLED, the container's half is run by hand: docker compose run --rm ci release generator-v<version>.

entities.title: Set up CI, deploys and releases (once)
entities.summary: The owner's one-time steps for the CI/CD container that replaced GitHub Actions.
entities.when: Once, when GitHub Actions is left (decision leave-github-actions), or when the container moves to another machine.
steps: On a machine with Docker that stays on: clone continuous_integration_and_delivery and cd cyberspace-explorer
Make a fine-grained GitHub token for this repository only, with Contents: read and Commit statuses: read and write; save it as secrets/github_token
Make a second fine-grained token for this repository only, with Contents: read and write, for releases; save it as secrets/github_release_token

Make a Cloudflare API token with Workers Scripts: Edit, D1: Edit, Workers R2 Storage: Edit and Queues: Edit on the account, and Workers Routes: Edit and DNS: Edit on the zone cyberspace-explorer.com; save it as secrets/cloudflare_api_token. The repository secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN can't be read back from GitHub, so this is a new token (or the owner's own copy of the old one)
cp .env.example .env, then docker compose up -d --build
In this repository's settings on GitHub: Actions → General → Disable actions; delete the repository secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (and the old token on Cloudflare, if it is not reused)
In the branch protection (or ruleset) of main, make ci/cyberspace-explorer a required status check, in place of the checks test and rust
Set DEPLOY_ENABLED=true and RELEASE_ENABLED=true in .env, then docker compose up -d
entities.verify: docker compose logs shows the container watching this repository; the next commit on a branch gets the status ci/cyberspace-explorer, and the next green main gets deploy/cyberspace-explorer.
entities.details: The container's README says the same at more length, with what must come first on Cloudflare: icelander.net's login service (before REQUIRE_SIGN_IN is set to "true") and the crawler's resources (crawler/README.md). Until GitHub Actions is off, keep DEPLOY_ENABLED and RELEASE_ENABLED false, or both would deploy main and both would make a tag's release. continuous_integration_and_delivery is a private repository.
